# Governance Proposals Reference

Complete reference for the `glassfrog proposal` command group — the governance
write flow (create, propose, respond, withdraw) and its two API reads (list,
get). The group also hosts the client-less `grammar` knowledge read, documented
separately in [Change-Set Grammar](change-set-grammar.md).

## Overview

`glassfrog proposal` is a non-runnable command group. Running `glassfrog
proposal` with no subcommand prints help. It hosts six verb leaves that call the
API:

| Command | API operation | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `proposal create <tension-id>` | `POST /proposals` | Create a draft proposal anchored to a tension |
| `proposal list` | `GET /proposals` | List the proposals visible to the caller |
| `proposal get <prp-id>` | `GET /proposals/{id}` | Read one proposal with full detail |
| `proposal propose <prp-id>` | `POST /proposals/{id}/propose` | Advance a draft into circulation |
| `proposal respond <prp-id>` | `POST /proposals/{id}/responses` | Record a consent response |
| `proposal withdraw <prp-id>` | `POST /proposals/{id}/withdraw` | Return a circulating proposal to draft |

plus one leaf that calls nothing:

| Command | API operation | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `proposal grammar` | **none** | Show what a proposal's `changes[]` may say — see [Change-Set Grammar](change-set-grammar.md) |

**Premium gating**: the four write verbs (`create`, `propose`, `respond`,
`withdraw`) require the async-proposals Premium feature. When it is not enabled,
the API answers `403` and the command surfaces it as a permission failure. The
two API reads (`list`, `get`) are **not** Premium-gated and answer on any plan,
and `grammar` reaches no endpoint at all.

Codebase enrichment skipped — not attempted. This reference is based on the
interface contracts only.

## `glassfrog proposal create` — create a draft proposal

### Synopsis

```
glassfrog proposal create <TENSION_ID> --changes <SOURCE> [--base-url URL] [-o FORMAT]
```

Sends `POST /proposals` and produces the created proposal, including its `prp_`
id and `draft` status.

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TENSION_ID` | string | yes | The anchor tension the proposal is raised against (`ten_…`), sent as `proposal.tension_id`. Exactly one required (cobra `ExactArgs(1)`); zero or more than one is a usage error with no API call. Not validated locally — the API resolves it (an unknown or malformed id returns `404`/`422`). |

### Write flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--changes` | string | — | **Required.** The governance change set, a JSON array, resolved from one of three sources: the reserved keyword `stdin` (any casing) reads the array from piped standard input; a value that resolves to an existing regular file reads the array from that file; any other value is treated as the inline JSON array itself. A file literally named `stdin` is reachable as `./stdin`. A missing `--changes` is a usage error, before any request. |

The change set is validated against a minimal floor before any request: it must
be valid JSON, a non-empty array, and every element must be an object carrying a
non-empty `type`. Beyond that floor, every command-specific key is passed
through to the server **verbatim** — the CLI reads only each element's `type`,
never its other keys, and performs no per-change-type validation.

`create` exposes no per-change-type builders, no proposer flag (the API derives
the proposer from the token), no status flag (the API creates the proposal in
`draft`), and no `--if-match`/concurrency flag (a create has no prior `ETag`).

## `glassfrog proposal list` — list proposals

### Synopsis

```
glassfrog proposal list [--status STATUS] [--role-id ROLE_ID] [--proposer-id PERSON_ID]
                        [--proposed-after TIMESTAMP] [--accepted-after TIMESTAMP]
                        [--first-page] [--per-page N] [--base-url URL] [-o FORMAT]
```

`proposal list` takes no positional argument — the list is global, and the
circle is the optional `--role-id` filter. Any positional is a usage error. It
walks every page to completion by default.

### List flags

Supplied filters combine; each is sent as its own query parameter. With no
filter, every proposal visible to the caller is requested.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--status` | string | — | Filter by proposal status, sent as `status`. **Validated locally** against the proposal status set; an unsupported value is a usage error naming the value and the supported set, with no API call. `--status ""` behaves as no filter. |
| `--role-id` | string | — | Filter to proposals in the circle supported by this role, sent as `role_id`. Passed through unvalidated; a malformed value surfaces as the API's `400`. |
| `--proposer-id` | string | — | Filter to proposals created by this person, sent as `proposer_id`. Passed through unvalidated. |
| `--proposed-after` | string | — | Only proposals with `proposed_at` on or after this timestamp, sent as `proposed_after`. Passed through unvalidated (the API validates the timestamp shape). |
| `--accepted-after` | string | — | Only proposals with `accepted_at` on or after this timestamp, sent as `accepted_after`. Passed through unvalidated. |
| `--first-page` | bool | false | Fetch only the first page and signal on stderr if more exist, rather than walking every page. |
| `--per-page` | int | API max (500) | Page size for the walk; the API owns the valid range. |

### Supported `--status` values

`draft`, `proposed_outside_meeting`, `escalated`, `accepted`,
`draft_with_conflicts`.

### Completeness

- **Default** — walks every page and renders the complete set.
- **`--first-page`** — issues a single page request; if more pages exist, writes
  `note: more proposals exist than shown; re-run without --first-page to fetch all`
  to stderr and exits `0`.
- **Mid-walk failure** — renders the proposals gathered so far, writes
  `note: result is incomplete — <cause>; the proposals shown are a partial set`
  to stderr, and exits non-zero. A partial list is never silently presented as
  complete.

## `glassfrog proposal get` — read a single proposal

### Synopsis

```
glassfrog proposal get <PRP_ID> [--base-url URL] [-o FORMAT]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PRP_ID` | string | yes | The proposal to read (`prp_…`). Exactly one required. Passed through unvalidated; an unknown or invisible id returns `404`. |

`get` declares no list flags — passing any of `--status`, `--role-id`,
`--proposer-id`, `--proposed-after`, `--accepted-after`, `--first-page`, or
`--per-page` is a usage error. The single read is unpaginated.

The read produces the proposal's `changes[]` (each `type` plus free-form
properties, rendered verbatim), the aggregate `response_summary` (counts only —
no per-person attribution), and the `available_transitions` the caller may
invoke. `available_transitions` is descriptive data — the read surfaces the
names but never auto-invokes a transition.

## `glassfrog proposal propose` — advance a draft into circulation

### Synopsis

```
glassfrog proposal propose <PRP_ID> [--base-url URL] [-o FORMAT]
```

Sends a bodyless `POST /proposals/{id}/propose` and produces the advanced
proposal the server returns — now `proposed_outside_meeting`, carrying the
server-set `response_deadline`, the proposer's auto-recorded implicit
`no_objection`, and updated `available_transitions`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PRP_ID` | string | yes | The proposal to advance (`prp_…`). Exactly one required. Passed through unvalidated; an unknown or invisible id's `404` is a failure here. |

**Flags**: none. The transition takes no request body and no field flags, no
confirmation/`--force`/`--yes` flag, and no pre-check affordance — the server
authorizes the transition (a `422` when `propose` is not in
`available_transitions`); the command never pre-reads the proposal.

`404` and `422` are real failures, never success end-states — an advance has no
idempotent re-run.

## `glassfrog proposal respond` — record a consent response

### Synopsis

```
glassfrog proposal respond <PRP_ID> --response <VALUE> [--base-url URL] [-o FORMAT]
```

Sends `POST /proposals/{id}/responses` and produces the recorded response,
including its `prr_` id and the parent proposal's status at the time of response.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PRP_ID` | string | yes | The circulating proposal to respond to (`prp_…`). Exactly one required. Passed through unvalidated; an unknown or invisible id returns `404`. |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--response` | string | — | **Required.** The consent value, validated locally before any request against the supported set. An omitted value is a usage error naming `--response` as required and listing the supported values. |

### Supported `--response` values

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `no_objection` | Willing to let the proposal pass as written. When every expected responder has no-objection, the server auto-accepts. |
| `bring_to_meeting` | Wants live discussion. Persists on the proposal and blocks auto-acceptance. |

The responding person is the token's own identity — the command supplies no
person field. When the recorded response triggers auto-acceptance, the parent
proposal's status in the result reads `accepted`. A second response by the same
person returns `422` and is surfaced as a generic API error — never retried.

## `glassfrog proposal withdraw` — return a circulating proposal to draft

### Synopsis

```
glassfrog proposal withdraw <PRP_ID> [--base-url URL] [-o FORMAT]
```

The mirror of `propose`. Sends a bodyless `POST /proposals/{id}/withdraw` and
produces the withdrawn proposal — now back in `draft`, with `proposed_at` and
`response_deadline` cleared and prior responses deleted server-side.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PRP_ID` | string | yes | The circulating proposal to withdraw (`prp_…`). Exactly one required. Passed through unvalidated; an unknown or invisible id's `404` is a failure here. |

**Flags**: none — same shape as `propose`. No request body, no confirmation
flag, no pre-check. `404` and `422` (the proposal is already `draft`, or
`withdraw` is not in `available_transitions`) are real failures. The withdraw
deletes existing responses server-side, but the command never prompts for
confirmation and never narrates that side effect — it surfaces only the returned
proposal.

## Inherited flags

Every leaf inherits the persistent root flags by cobra inheritance:

| Flag | Owner | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--base-url` | 011 | Override the API base URL (top rung of the base-URL precedence chain). |
| `-o`, `--output` | 020/035 | `full` (default) \| `compact` \| `json` \| `yaml` \| a user-template ref. |

Successful output is rendered by Output Format Selection in the resolved format:
`json`/`yaml` emit the structured `{data: …}` document verbatim; `full`/`compact`
render the human projection. The raw API envelope is never emitted under a human
format, and no command defines its own format flag. Each command produces
structured data and synthesizes no fields the server did not return.

`grammar` is the one exception to the envelope sentence, and deliberately so: it
has no server response to mirror, so its `json`/`yaml` output is the reference
structure itself. Its `--base-url` also parses and is inert. See
[Change-Set Grammar](change-set-grammar.md).

## Proposal status lifecycle

A proposal moves through server-owned states. The CLI never sets or recomputes
status — it surfaces whatever the server returns.

```
draft ──propose──▶ proposed_outside_meeting ──(all no-objection)──▶ accepted
  ▲                          │
  └────────withdraw──────────┘
```

`escalated` and `draft_with_conflicts` are additional statuses the `--status`
filter accepts.

## Error reference

Failure rendering is format-aware: for `json`/`yaml` the unified error envelope
is written to stdout; for `full`/`compact` the diagnostic (cause + next step) is
written to stderr. Every diagnostic names the cause and a next step and never
includes the token. Only `create` introduces an exit code of its own — the
invalid-create code `8`, below; every other proposal command draws entirely on
the shared convention.

| Condition | Outcome | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| Success | Success | 0 |
| Missing/extra positional, missing required flag, malformed `--changes`, empty change set, change without `type`, unsupported `--status`/`--response`, list flag on `get`, unknown flag, invalid `--output`, base-URL config error | UsageError | 2 |
| No usable token | UsageError | 2 |
| Unreadable/malformed credential file, render failure | RuntimeError | 1 |
| Unknown anchor tension/proposal (`404`), rejected change or field (`422`), transition not allowed (`422`), other `4xx`/`5xx`, response shape mismatch | APIError | 3 |
| Async proposals not enabled (`403`), other permission (`401`) | PermissionError | 4 |
| Rate limited (`429`) — write verbs are not auto-retried | RateLimited | 5 |
| Could not reach the wire | NetworkUnavailable | 6 |
| `create` only: the server accepted the create and reports the created draft not valid | InvalidCreate | 8 |

The table above covers the six API leaves. `grammar` can produce only `0`, `2`,
and `1`; codes `3`–`6` and `8` are unproducible for it because it issues no
request. Code `8` is reachable from `create` alone: it is the one outcome that
follows a write the server *accepted*, so no read and no other write verb has a
state it could describe.

The Premium `403` classifies as `PermissionError` (4) with the server's detail
surfaced. The command adds no plan-aware "not available on your plan"
interpretation — that distinction belongs to a separate Plan-Limit Signal
capability.
